content.text: Two findings. The barrels and fence landed, but `bed()` refused both beds. Stored air in this build is the namespaced `minecraft:air`, and the library's air check (`/(^|_)air$/`) doesn't match it, so `bed()` treats every shell-filled cell as occupied. That is a library bug and it will block the real room too. For the scratch copy I'll place the bed halves directly and read the full room output.

input.summary:
P0 west bedroom lamps: two standing lanterns at (3,7,15) on the fence post and (3,7,19) on the south barrel, guarded at the end of parts/room-6.mjs build(g). Scratch copy with the designer's furniture stand-in reads min 12, 0 dark, 0 dim, walk and fit OK.
The real build has no furniture in this room yet, so the lamps write nothing (guard skips them). Real-build light is still min 6, no dark cell.
make.sh rebuilds build.nbt; room-6 placed 0, refused 0.
left: Real-build light not confirmed at min 12: P0 west bedroom has no furniture in build.nbt yet (room-6 build(g) is still empty), so the real map reads min 6 with 6 dim cells and no dark cell. Re-run `mcd room build.nbt --rooms rooms.json --only "P0 west bedroom"` once the designer's furniture is placed.

shell-west fills the whole interior with stored air, and runParts locks those cells, so every room write (furniture and my lanterns) is refused in the real build. Needs the shell to leave the interior cells unowned (shell-west owner's fix). Until then the lamp guard is a no-op by design.

bed() in the build library refuses stored "minecraft:air" cells: its air test /(^|_)air$/ does not match the namespace, so every bed in a shell-filled room returns false silently. I placed the scratch beds by hand and did not change the library (outside this part).
The bedroom has no ceiling block at y9 in the build, so hanging lanterns are not possible here; both lamps stand on furniture.

The designer's plan (three lanterns, one on the north barrel at z14) also reads min 12 on the scratch copy; I dropped the z14 lantern as not needed (two lanterns, min 12). The designer should confirm that choice.

waste.what: Found the smallest lantern set reaching min 12 by building a scratch copy with the designer's furniture by hand, then measuring five lantern sets one at a time.
waste.cost: ~3 scratch scripts, 2 failed builds (bed() refused, so beds were set cell by cell), 5 measured variants
waste.tool: A `mcd room --try "x,y,z ..."` (or a minimal-lamp search to a target min, e.g. --min 12) that tries lantern sets on a copy of build.nbt and reports the min. The current suggestion lists one lamp only (lifts dim cells to 8+), which can't reach 12 here.

waste.what: Hand-set both bed halves on the scratch copy because bed() silently refused the cells.
waste.cost: 2 bed calls refused, 2 manual set() pairs written, 1 library read to find the cause
waste.tool: Fix bed()'s air test in build.mjs to accept "minecraft:air" (use g.isAir); until fixed, every bed in a shell-filled room is refused with no warning.

waste.what: Worked out the lamp's support cell and the empty-cell rule (feet layer y6 supported by the layer below, head layer y7 on the furniture) by reading probe output cell by cell.
waste.tool: `mcd room` could report, for each lantern spot, the block it stands on and whether that block is furniture yet, and warn when a lamp call would float.

companions.task: Place the room's furniture the designer laid out (barrel dressers at z14 and z19-20, fence table at x3 z15, two beds at z17-18 with heads at x3), so the lamp guard has supports to light from.
Leave the P0 west bedroom interior cells (x3..4, z14..20, y6..8) unowned instead of filling them with stored air, so the room's furniture and lanterns can be written at all.
